messages:
danielle.arch: FYI I sketched an operational cadence for the "stitchless" refactor initiative — goal: pay down service coupling while keeping launch velocity.
omar.eng: curious about the cadence. short cuts or long runway?
danielle.arch: Proposal:
- Discovery sprint (1w): map hotpaths + synchronous call graph
- Micro-work sprints (4 x 2w): each targets a tiny bounded extraction + adapter
- Convergence sprint (1w): QA, canaries, rollback rehearsals
- Continuous paydown: biweekly debt review + metrics refresh
rachel.pm: who owns acceptance? we need product gates for behavior parity.
danielle.arch: product owns acceptance tests for user-visible routes; infra owns route toggles and canary plumbing; eng teams own adapters and migration tests.
omar.eng: technical note: prefer small, reversible extractions. each extraction must include an integration harness and a replayable trace set. keep PRs <500 LOC.
danielle.arch: metrics to track: sync-call ratio, cross-service p95, number of endpoints with dual-write, and blocked refactor tickets. target: 25% reduction in sync calls by quarter end.
rachel.pm: add stakeholder comms cadence. weekly triage and a short public status for impacted teams.
sre-bot: Reminder: schedule proxy toggle feature flag 2w before planned canary start.
omar.eng: also add a soft SLA for adapter parity tests: 96% pass on CI for 3 consecutive runs before canary.
danielle.arch: agreed. I'll post the RFC with timeline and a simple checklist: discovery artefacts, adapter harness, parity tests, canary plan, rollback playbook. tagging eng leads for review.
rachel.pm: thanks — i'll slot this into next Wed ops sync and coordinate product freezes.
danielle.arch: thanks team, will iterate on feedback and push RFC link here when ready.
